title: Strange Talon
dek: An Owlin intelligence chief who bargains for knowledge, kills Swift Foot during a public confrontation and later defeats Ghilsen. His institutional grievances and increasingly broad hostility remain beside the precise acts the quests record.

facts.Last dated scene in dossier: 8 June 2025 · fatal duel with Ghilsen; Talon survives the encounter

body:
Strange Talon, the Rahu Master of Intelligence, can welcome a visitor, notice a trinket and offer a price for useful knowledge. He also kills Swift Foot in front of the embassy’s workers and later answers Ghilsen’s challenge with a fatal duel. His service to Witch Queen Ephraith joins an intelligence officer’s watchfulness to increasingly bitter dealings with adventurers.

18 June 2024: conditional hospitality

At an aviary or outpost, Talon initially receives the Pristinian visitors with watchful curiosity. Rahu-controlled space is open to guests who respect its rules; welcome does not imply unrestricted access or permanent trust. He notices what adventurers carry and asks where their knowledge came from.

His exchanges with Scribonia show this earlier Talon clearly. He already has reports of Scribonia’s encounters with dangerous magic, offers payment for information and samples, and argues that mutually useful knowledge deserves reciprocal exchange. He can bargain, explain, and engage intellectually. Suspicion has not yet become an indiscriminate refusal to speak.

Knowledge, discipline, and honor

Talon treats information as a resource that should be acquired deliberately and disclosed selectively. His conception of honor joins obligation, reputation, cultural law, and the consequences of breaking agreements. Rahu discipline does not require rejecting wealth or abundance; it requires control over desire and attention to proper use.

These are Talon’s expressed values and Rahu positions. They do not make him an omniscient witness, establish that every Rahu historical claim is objective truth, or remove his capacity for bias.

The assault that changes the relationship

After Swift Foot’s death, the visitors who approach on 7 August 2024 see a wound on Talon’s arm and encounter his explicit hostility. He accuses adventurers of trying to kill him and then questioning his honor. Yet apology, compensation, and a declaration that the group had not collectively endorsed the attack still produce a change: he asks why they had not said so earlier and wants the offender denounced.

His grievance concerns the response of a community as well as the actions of an attacker. Recognition of the offense and meaningful repudiation can still matter. He can also acknowledge an enemy’s combat skill while condemning how that skill was used.

May 2025: grievance becomes a political argument

When Magnus Niriin meets him in May, Talon’s scars visibly speak to pain. He directs Magnus toward the histories of Aravil and Ithilrûnë and accuses the adventuring community of protecting them.

Ask about Aravil and Ithilrune some time. You will know. Your kind protected them.Strange Talon

“Your kind” marks the widening of a specific injury into suspicion of a whole class. Talon’s position is that the community closes ranks when its members violate Rahu law. The biography preserves this as his interpretation rather than a verdict on every adventurer. Sophina’s competent diplomacy and Talon’s grievance together form part of the visible pathway by which Magnus moves closer to the Rahu.

June 2025: custody and direct combat

On 4 June, Magnus returns from the covert abduction of Melian and reports to Strange Talon with her in custody. Scout Lilian and Herb have been killed during the operation. Talon’s position at the receiving end establishes senior authority within the Rahu operation.

Receiving Melian does not establish that Talon designed the kidnapping, ordered the killing of witnesses, or knew every tactical detail in advance. Magnus’s documented field orders retain their own attribution.

On 8 June, Talon accepts a direct challenge, tells others not to interfere, allows the guards to move aside, and steps forward to fight. The intelligence chief who once preferred observation and negotiation now confronts the adventurers personally. The duel’s immediate outcome is recorded in the primary narration below.

The institutions and people around him

  • Witch Queen Ephraith: Talon’s sovereign. His loyalty is established; a family connection, romance, rivalry, or her approval of each decision is not.
  • Ambassador Sophina: the diplomatic counterpart who turns his grievance into a formal Rahu legal demand. Their professional alignment does not require an invented private friendship.
  • Captain Hildethrax: a senior military figure with overlapping state responsibilities. Intelligence, diplomacy, and military logistics are distinguishable functions, without a complete recovered constitutional chart.
  • Olokun: an early participant in a matter of justice and later an antagonist in disputes about Rahu honor.
  • Scribonia: a source of strategically valuable knowledge and a reminder that Talon could engage constructively before grievance dominated his dealings.

The open record

Talon’s age, earlier life, appointment, complete informant network, the complete allocation of acts in the Aravil/Ithilrûnë grievance, the Queen’s private judgment, and his fate after the duel remain unresolved. His history joins a real grievance to increasingly broad hostility without treating either pain or honor as proof that every later choice was justified.

A quiet moment at the embassy

At the Longest Night gathering, Cecil and Strange Talon discuss thought, action and the fleeting reflection of stars in the koi pond. Their conversation ends when a cry and splash interrupt the evening. Cecil goes to offer medical help and Talon flies toward the disturbance. Their shared contemplation gives way to duty.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

A welcome with watchful eyes

Talon’s first recovered embassy reception gives Scribonia an immediate reason for caution. The intelligence chief already knows of his experience in the Before, probes what he learned and offers to buy knowledge or samples. When Scribonia wants to understand his hosts before sharing, Talon accepts the delay while arguing that withholding mutually useful information would be dishonorable. He is trying to obtain something, not merely exchanging pleasantries.

He is less assured about Olokun’s shell-like trinket. He notices it, presses for its origin and struggles to remember a manifest. His own scene narration admits that a mistaken accusation would bring shame, so he signals Hildethrax to finish the visit. The watchful official has informants and a sharp eye, but an incomplete memory still limits what he can establish.

The demonstration and the ceremonial blade

Swift Foot enters the embassy grounds hoping to challenge the workers’ acceptance of their position. After speaking to Ummo, he finds Talon inspecting the grounds and attacks from concealment. Swift’s stated intention is to wound him as a demonstration. Once the attack lands, Swift throws down his sword, tells the watching workers that their protectors hold no special power, and claims responsibility for himself alone. He explicitly separates Melian and Pristinia from his act.

Talon covers himself in darkness and strikes with daggers and arrows. Swift deliberately stops defending himself and continues speaking. Talon says that Swift will die for challenging a master, then closes with a ceremonial blade. The narrator confirms the beheading. The killing follows a real attack, but the witnessed sequence also includes Swift’s discarded weapon, words and refusal to continue the fight.

Talon goes to report to his superiors. The servants take Swift’s body for a ceremonial burial and leave the blood on the rocks in his honor. The narrator names him a martyr and says the witnesses will remember and talk. Talon has killed his attacker; the observed aftermath does not show that he has silenced the questions Swift meant to raise.

Sophina carries another grievance to the council

At the council convened by Melian Starguard on 20 January 2025, Ambassador Sophina presents the Rahu account: Talon was magically compelled and prevented from performing his duty on Rahu land, then nearly killed when he confronted those involved. She characterizes the offenses as compulsion, obstruction of justice, and attempted murder, and says Rahu law requires death.

Aravil and Ithilrûnë are central to this grievance. The accounts does not assign every described act to both people individually. Sophina’s legal framing, Talon’s account, and the unresolved allocation of specific actions remain distinct.

The council allegations concern Aravil and Ithilrûnë. They remain distinct from Swift Foot’s fatal demonstration and the discussion following it. Talon’s later account of Swift’s attack says there was little talking; the direct embassy sequence preserves the words exchanged before Swift died. The discrepancy remains visible rather than being resolved by treating Talon’s later recollection as the whole encounter.

The accepted challenge ends in a death

During the fighting at Pristinia, Ghilsen taunts the Rahu and challenges someone to face him alone. Talon steps forward. He insists that the guards visibly move aside and that nobody else interfere before he climbs to the wall. The agreement to fight is witnessed; the record does not supply a complete exchange of every blow.

The narrator then states that Talon drops Ghilsen and leaves the corpse with a smirk before flying back toward the commotion. This resolves the duel’s immediate outcome: Talon survives and Ghilsen dies. Ghilsen’s later revival belongs to a subsequent chapter of his own history. It does not make this encounter nonfatal or establish Talon’s fate after the battle.

profile.personality: Observant, proud and capable of bargaining, contemplation and abrupt violence. His accusation against adventurers widens beyond named offenders; his later version of Swift’s attack leaves out words retained in the direct scene.
profile.achievements: Receives embassy visitors, offers payment for strategically useful knowledge, watches Rahu access and receives Melian in custody after Magnus’s operation. Kills Swift Foot and wins the fatal duel with Ghilsen. Receiving a captive does not prove that he ordered every act of the kidnapping.
profile.relationships: Ephraith is his sovereign; Sophina turns Rahu grievances into formal diplomatic demands. Hildethrax cooperates in access and investigation. Scribonia offers valuable knowledge, Olokun tests his patience, Magnus encounters his scars and hostility, and Cecil shares a brief contemplative conversation before duty interrupts.
